title: EATF Action Evidence Package toolkit
description: Open toolkit for creating, inspecting, and offline-verifying Action Evidence Packages (.aep): a hybrid RSA-4096 plus ML-DSA-65 signer, two verifiers (TypeScript and Python), both built by Tyche Institute, sign/verify/inspect CLIs, RFC 9881 public-key encoding, JSON schemas, positive and negative conformance vectors, and a deterministic offline downgrade lab.
notes: Version 0.7.0 adds a caller-supplied ML-DSA-65 signer-key pin (--pqc-signer-key, trustedPqcSignerPems, trusted_pqc_signer_pems; new failure code PQC_SIGNER_NOT_TRUSTED). Through v0.6.1 the embedded ML-DSA-65 key was not authenticated, so --require-pqc proved only that some ML-DSA-65 key signed the canonical bytes. A pin implies the required policy, and --require-pqc without a pin now warns. The deterministic lab adds a foreign-key package and a pinned policy: across seven packages and three policies, the two verifiers (TypeScript and Python, both built by Tyche Institute) return the same verdict and first-failure code for all 42 observations, and the 24 v0.6.1 observations are unchanged. Both verifiers now parse ML-DSA-65 PEM text by the same rules, and a cubic-time backtracking pattern in that parser (v0.6.0 and v0.6.1) is replaced by a linear one that accepts the same text. Native-Windows Python conformance now counts the 5 accepted and 8 rejected vectors instead of passing on none. Version DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23451134. Previous version v0.6.1 is doi:10.5281/zenodo.21763768 under concept doi:10.5281/zenodo.21763055; releases through v0.5.0 remain under earlier concept doi:10.5281/zenodo.21511608.
